newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Comcel posts $5.8 mln first-half loss.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Comcel posts $5.8 mln first-half loss.

text.p: Colombian cellular phone company Comcel posted a first-half net loss of $5.8 million (6.3 billion pesos) compared with a $2.4 million net profit in the same period last year, the company said in a statement Monday.

But Comcel said it had maintained its position as Colombia's market leader by more than doubling its subscriber base by the end of June to 239,317 users compared with 106,250 at the same time last year.
Comcel said first-half revenue rose to $117 million (127.6 billion pesos) from $71.7 million (78.2 billion pesos) in the first six months of 1996.
Operating income for the first half of 1997 jumped to $14 million from $4.7 million in the same period last year.
The Comcel statement said the company's accumulated long-term debt to the end of June stood at $350.3 million.

The company's controlling shareholders are Colombia's national phone company Empresa Nacional de Telecomunicaciones, regional phone company Empresa de Telecomunicaciones de Santafe de Bogota and Bell Canada International Inc
